questions: Did slalom progress rise above 0.34 or produce any finishes, compared with iteration 3 (0.34, 0 finishes) and iteration 5 (0.15)?
Did s-bend and oval finish rates hold near iteration 3 (0.30 and 0.85) at 0.5 kg?
Did s-bend steering_oscillation rise above about 0.5 (iteration 3: 0.44), indicating the lower inertia is overshooting?
If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at about 0.06 m, is the remaining limit the controller's kd or base_speed rather than geometry?

intent: Return to the iteration-3 geometry, the best design so far (493.2), and test only lower yaw inertia by reducing mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.34 with some slalom finishes, s-bend and oval finish rates at or above iteration 3 (0.30 and 0.85), and steering_oscillation staying below about 0.5 on the s-bend.
learning: Iteration 5 showed that wider outer sensors (+/-0.07 m, 23 mm spacing) remove slalom line loss but cut slalom and s-bend progress, so sensor reach is not the slalom limit. Iteration 4 showed that narrowing the track to 0.08 m hurts every track. The remaining levers on geometry are yaw inertia (mass) and possibly footprint size. If mass 0.5 kg does not improve the slalom, the next test is a 12 mm footprint at the iteration-3 span, and any further turn change is handed to the Integrator as controller gains (kd, base_speed).
rationale: Iteration 5 widened the outer sensors to +/-0.07 m and scored 430.1, below iteration 3's 493.2. Slalom line loss fell to 0.0, which confirms the reach change did what it was meant to do. But slalom progress fell from 0.34 to 0.15 and the s-bend finish rate fell from 0.30 to 0.10, with s-bend progress down from 0.75 to 0.71. Wider reach therefore does not fix the slalom, and it appears to cost progress on the other tracks. The 0.07 m span is rejected. I return the sensor array to the iteration-3 layout (7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.05 m) and the 0.10 m track, which together gave the best score so far. The slalom still ends with max_error about 0.062, at the 0.06 m off-track floor, which the body width cannot change. Iteration 3 showed that lowering yaw inertia restored s-bend progress, and the slalom is the remaining failure. So I reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg with the body unchanged, which cuts yaw inertia by about 17 percent. This is the only change from iteration 3. Expected result: a slalom finish rate above zero or higher slalom progress, with oval and s-bend holding near iteration 3. Risk: lower inertia can add steering oscillation, so I request steering_oscillation on every track.
